findings.problem: The underlying fact is simple: if an ideal Q vanishes at a point `a` and contains `X i - C c`, then `c = a i`. The lemma states it only for index `0` of `Fin (m + 1)` and only when `a 0 = 1`. It also inherits `[Field C]` from the section, although its `omit` line already drops `CharZero` and `IsAlgClosed`. The proof uses only `eval_sub`, `eval_X`, `eval_C` and `sub_eq_zero`, and these hold over any commutative ring and any index type. The hypothesis `ha : a 0 = 1` is used only at the very end, to rewrite `a 0` as `1`. Because of these choices, the lemma cannot be applied to other coordinates or other centre values.
findings.proposed_change:
State the general lemma first and keep the current one as a corollary:

```lean
theorem coordinate_sub_eval_mem_of_center {R σ : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (Q : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ R)) (a : σ → R) (i : σ)
    (hpoint : ∀ p ∈ Q, MvPolynomial.eval a p = 0)
    (hconstant : ∃ c : R, X i - MvPolynomial.C c ∈ Q) :
    X i - MvPolynomial.C (a i) ∈ Q := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hconstant
  have he := hpoint _ hc
  simp only [eval_sub, eval_X, eval_C, sub_eq_zero] at he
  simpa only [he] using hc
```

The proof is the existing one with `ha` and `map_one` removed. `he : a i = c`, so rewriting `hc` with it gives the goal. Then `constant_coordinate_eq_one_of_center` becomes `by simpa [ha] using coordinate_sub_eval_mem_of_center Q a 0 hpoint hconstant`, using `MvPolynomial.C 1 = 1`. The only existing caller (CurveComponentRigidity.lean, line 94) can keep using the corollary unchanged.

Degenerate cases: no condition on `R`, `σ` or `Q` is needed. If `Q = ⊤`, `hpoint` fails at `p = 1` whenever `R` is nontrivial, and if `R` is trivial everything holds anyway.
findings.benefit: Users get a reusable, field-free fact: an ideal that vanishes at a point determines the constant in any coordinate relation `X i - C c ∈ Q`. It covers every coordinate, every centre value and every coefficient ring, instead of only the normalised case `a 0 = 1` over a field indexed by `Fin (m + 1)`. The name and statement also describe the actual content. The current specialised form stays available as a short corollary.
